items.title: Implement computeWriteSet + globsOverlap in new core/parallel-decomposition-overlap.ts
items.context: Pure functions per spec 4.2: computeWriteSet(contract: ScopeContractData) returns created+modified paths; globsOverlap(a,b) does literal-path intersection + shared-dir-prefix heuristic + broadness (NARROW/BROAD over literal|dir/*|dir/**), returning GlobOverlapResult {overlap,pairs,broadSide}. Import types from parallel-decomposition.js. No I/O.
items.userSees: globsOverlap returns overlap=true with colliding pairs for literal-path overlap; computeWriteSet unions a contract allowedModify+allowedCreate; smoke prints PASS.

happy.desc: globsOverlap detects literal-path overlap (returns overlap=true + pairs) and computeWriteSet derives the union write-set

edge.desc: tier-2 shared-dir-prefix flags a possible overlap conservatively (dir/* vs dir/literal) without under-flagging

adversarial.desc: disjoint write-sets return overlap=false; a BROAD glob is flagged with correct broadSide attribution

verificationEvidence.note: Smoke PASS: globsOverlap detects literal-path overlap with colliding pairs; computeWriteSet unions allowedModify+allowedCreate+allowedTest deduped.

items.title: Add grammar validator + unit tests (parallel-decomposition-overlap.test.ts)
items.context: Validator rejects mid-path ** and bare top-level * at the write-set grammar boundary. Tests via a smoke script packages/main/src/tasks/parallel-decomposition-overlap-smoke.ts (repo convention: node dist/tasks/<name>-smoke.js; no .test.ts framework). Smoke covers: literal overlap, dir-prefix over-flag, BROAD classification + broadSide attribution, disjoint sets, grammar rejection. tsc + smoke green.
items.userSees: The grammar validator rejects mid-path ** and bare top-level *; node dist/tasks/parallel-decomposition-overlap-smoke.js prints PASS for all 5 behaviors.

happy.desc: grammar validator rejects mid-path ** and bare top-level *; smoke exits 0 (PASS) covering all 5 behaviors

edge.desc: NARROW vs BROAD classification is correct for literal / dir/* / dir/** below vs at package root

adversarial.desc: the smoke fails loudly (non-zero exit) if any assertion breaks — not a silent pass
